change: add-self-hosted-p2p-dsh-connections: pairing, connection staging, session isolation, remote project selection, shared server configuration, post-disconnect reconciliation and Run-page peer entry points
scope_note: Code-level gate for the desktop and Go implementation of self-hosted P2P DSH connections. Every command listed here was executed and passed. Physical two-machine acceptance (7.3), network matrix (7.4), failure matrix (7.5), four-architecture packaging (6.3), server deployment (6.1/6.2), full interactive ledger (5.9) and release evidence (7.7) are NOT covered and remain open: they require a second physical machine and a self-hosted coordination server. Remote directory semantics are proven against a real filesystem, never mocked path strings. The worktree also contains earlier in-progress P2P work from previous stages of this same change (accounts, enrollment, control-plane user management); those files are declared here so the manifest has no undeclared production surface, but their own stage gates own their evidence. Agent working notes under .agents/notes/ are not part of the product surface and are excluded.

state_matrix.test: pins the confirmed identity only once the server reports the pair active
does not pin when approval leaves the pair still pending
bounds one page and reports the total (TestBoundsOnePageAndReportsTotal)
lets a readback clear an unknown outcome so the user can proceed
blocks further writes after a write whose outcome is unknown
drops the entry point even when helper teardown fails
hands the entry point only for the matching generation
refuses a hand-written partition that this app never allocated
keeps the input and flags a conflict when the revision is stale
refuses the update while any computer sharing the service is busy
distinguishes a lost connection from a stopped task
refuses to reconnect a revoked pair and explains why

field_bindings.source: SHA-256 of the actual remote device public key received over the authenticated helper channel
field_bindings.test: derives the confirmation fingerprint from the real key rather than trusting the reply
field_bindings.assertion: a reply-supplied fingerprint is never displayed or trusted
field_bindings.missing_semantics: A mismatch between the confirmed value and the real key refuses approval; an identity substituted between confirmation and readback is rejected and never pinned.

field_bindings.source: authoritative pairs.identity readback after every write
field_bindings.test: reads back the authoritative record instead of trusting the invite write reply
field_bindings.missing_semantics: pending_target_approval and pending_initiator_confirmation are distinct from active; accepting an invite can never yield an active pair.

field_bindings.source: helper peer.connect reply, retained in main only
field_bindings.test: keeps the local DSH entry URL out of the returned state
field_bindings.assertion: no renderer-visible field can carry the entry URL
field_bindings.missing_semantics: An entry point from a superseded generation is refused; a failed teardown still drops the URL.

field_bindings.source: one-way derivation from the pinned serviceId and pairId
field_bindings.test: admits only the partition the intended identity derives to
field_bindings.assertion: another computer's partition is refused for this identity
field_bindings.missing_semantics: Renaming a computer does not move partitions; two computers never collide; the Local partition is never reused by a peer.

field_bindings.source: real target filesystem resolution via EvalSymlinks and filepath.Rel on the remote platform
field_bindings.assertion: resolved path outside the authorized root is refused, not clamped
field_bindings.missing_semantics: Containment is re-checked after resolution; traversal, foreign-root references and malformed references are refused; missing, forbidden and empty are distinct states.

field_bindings.source: opaque reference issued by the remote computer
field_bindings.test: refuses a reference that is not an opaque token
field_bindings.assertion: this side never builds a reference from a path
field_bindings.missing_semantics: A page larger than its request or the declared total is rejected; browsing requires a currently active pair.

field_bindings.source: service.configure reply verified against the already pinned public key
field_bindings.test: refuses an endpoint that resolves to a different service identity
field_bindings.assertion: a new address is accepted only when it proves the same pinned identity
field_bindings.missing_semantics: The whole affected computer set must be idle; a stale revision, unknown service, forgotten service or failed server call leaves the stored configuration byte-identical and triggers no reconnect.

field_bindings.source: live connection stages read back from the helper
field_bindings.test: does not clear the warning merely because the peer reconnected
field_bindings.assertion: a lost connection is never reported as a stopped or completed task
field_bindings.missing_semantics: connection_lost, work_unknown and runtime_replaced stay distinct; only an explicit user confirmation clears the warning; nothing is ever retried, resubmitted or inferred.

field_bindings.source: P2P catalog records plus live connection stages
field_bindings.test: never carries an address for a revoked pair
field_bindings.assertion: a revoked or disconnected peer tab can never hold a loadable address
field_bindings.missing_semantics: Tab identity follows the pair, not the display name, so a rename does not reload; a removed computer drops its tab and the active tab falls back to Local; the DSH entry point never enters tab state.

real_commands.command: npx vitest run electron/main/p2p/ electron/main/security.test.ts src/app/domains/remote-connections/

runtime_evidence.artifact: Real-filesystem directory semantics: networking/internal/runtimebridge/directory_test.go builds actual temp trees, symlinks and project markers; listing content is read back from the filesystem rather than asserted by array length.

OPEN: physical two-machine pairing, connection and remote project acceptance; four-architecture packaging; one-hour soak with real DSH HTTP/WS; release evidence. These require a second physical machine and a self-hosted coordination server and are not satisfied by any test in this gate.

User documentation (docs/p2p-connections.md and .zh-CN.md) states the no-relay limit, the authorized-root-is-not-a-DSH-sandbox distinction, and that an installer build is not a release. Every error code it documents was verified to exist in src/shared/p2p-management.ts or the Go tree.

tools/p2p-preflight.mjs was exercised against real endpoints on this machine: a genuine STUN Binding to stun.l.google.com:19302 succeeded, a dead UDP port timed out, an untrusted certificate (self-signed.badssl.com) was identified as a TLS trust failure, a real wss handshake completed, and a tampered helper binary was caught by checksum.

All 92 user-facing p2p error codes in src/shared/p2p-management.ts are explained in docs/p2p-connections.md and .zh-CN.md, enforced by tools/p2p-docs-coverage.test.mjs. The guard was verified to fail by name when an undocumented code is introduced.

acceptance_status: Not release-accepted. Implementation and code-level verification are complete and reproducible via real_commands. The interaction contract is authored but its ledger has NOT been produced: no raw interactive evidence exists yet, because every workflow requires a second physical computer and a deployed self-hosted server. implementation_complete remains false in the contract until that acceptance runs. Pre-existing unrelated failures in electron/main/pnpm-launcher.test.ts (Windows pnpm shim) are outside this manifest and were confirmed to fail independently of these changes.
